topic: Variadic Templates and Parameter Pack Expansion for Utilities
explanation: Variadic templates in C++ allow functions or classes to accept a variable number of arguments, making code more flexible and reusable. This is particularly useful in real-world scenarios like implementing logging functions, processing variable-length data, or creating generic utilities (e.g., in libraries like fmt or std::format). Best practices include using recursion for older C++ standards (pre-C++17) to unpack parameter packs, ensuring a clear base case to avoid infinite recursion, and preferring fold expressions in C++17+ for simpler, more efficient code. Common pitfalls include stack overflows from deep recursion (mitigated by limiting argument counts or using C++17 features), forgetting to handle all types in the pack (which can lead to compilation errors), and overusing variadics when simpler overloads suffice—always profile for performance as recursion adds overhead.
